newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens sees rail unit gains in 1998/99.
newsitem.headline: Siemens sees rail unit gains in 1998/99.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens AG predicted a dramatic turnaround in its rail technology unit in 1998/99, exceeding even the most optimistic analysts' forecasts.
Siemens said it expected the transportation technology (VT) unit's 1998/99 sales to reach about six billion marks, up from 4.3 billion marks in 1995/96, which ended last September.
Unit chief Wolfram Martinsen, speaking to reporters on Tuesday evening, also predicted a "giant leap" in group profit in the next two years, after 19 million marks in pretax profit last year.
The sharp rise will come as the unit puts behind it the high costs of restructuring and start-ups for major projects that it has experienced in the past few years, Martinsen said.
Peter Roe, who follows Siemens for Banque Paribas in London, said, "I'm a little surprised about the size of the figures but it's quite possible. The outlook for transportation is very good."
Roe forecast 1998/99 VT sales of 5.2 billion.
In the first half of this year, VT sales fell 11 percent to 1.6 billion marks while orders rose 46 percent to 3.2 billion marks.
The group has suffered from fierce competition that depressed prices for rail projects. "For a while the big orders dried up and the margins in the industry were very, very poor," Roe said.
He expected VT to gain now that demand was showing signs of firming. "They have also done a lot of rationalising that should help their results," he said.
Martinsen said Siemens was seeing uninterrupted demand for rail systems, especially in Asia, and expected annual world market growth of about seven percent.
In Asia, more and more contracts were being awarded for turnkey projects that require a general contractor to offer financial as well as construction services.
